title: 有些人的名字不能提  (Some Names Must Not Be Spoken)

segments.t: At her new desk, Bu Xiaogu wins over exhausted assistant Xiaoye with a cup of sour-plum soda — only to learn that nobody dares speak Chun Yuqiao's name aloud in the office. Listen first.
这杯苏打水是我熬夜的利器。
尝一下，尝了准不后悔！
请问，淳于总在哪儿？
求别说！
怎么了？
有些人的名字不能提，你提到他，他就会出现。
我们累到没有时间去写辞职信。
你是联合制作人的助理，跟我们不一样。
怎么不一样？
因为我们不用和他开会！
Let's unpack their deskside chat. Xiaogu breaks the ice by sharing her favourite late-night drink.
这杯苏打水是我熬夜的利器。

'This cup of soda water is my secret weapon for staying up late.' Every student and TV editor knows "aoye", literally 'boil the night', for pulling an all-nighter, and "liqi" means a sharp tool or secret weapon.
尝一下，尝了准不后悔！
'Have a taste — once you try it, you definitely will not regret it!' Soft "yixia" after "chang", 'taste', makes the offer casual, while colloquial "zhun" means 'for sure' before "houhui", 'regret'.
请问，淳于总在哪儿？

'Excuse me, where is Director Chun Yu?' Always start a polite question to a colleague or stranger with "qingwen", literally 'please let me ask', and put company title "zong", 'director', after the surname.
求别说！
'Please, do not say it!' Dramatic internet-era shorthand "qiu", 'beg', plus "bie", 'don't', packs 'I beg you, don't say a word!' into three panicked syllables.
怎么了？
'What is wrong?' Two words to memorise as one unit: "zenme le" asks 'what happened?' or 'what is the matter?' whenever someone suddenly looks alarmed.
有些人的名字不能提，你提到他，他就会出现。
'Some people's names must not be mentioned; if you mention him, he will appear.' Here "buneng" expresses what is forbidden or unsafe to do, and "ti" means bring up a name or topic.
我们累到没有时间去写辞职信。
'We are so tired that we have no time to write a resignation letter.' Putting "dao" right after "lei", 'tired', shows how far the exhaustion goes, and "cizhixin" is a resignation letter.
你是联合制作人的助理，跟我们不一样。
'You are the co-producer's assistant — you are different from us.' Here comes our comparison chunk "bu yiyang" again, paired with "zhuli", the everyday workplace word for an assistant.
怎么不一样？
'How am I different?' Putting "zenme" directly in front of "bu yiyang" asks 'in what way not the same?' — a crisp follow-up you can use in any conversation.
因为我们不用和他开会！

'Because we do not have to attend meetings with him!' Watch the difference between "buneng" ('cannot') and "buyong" ('do not need to'), while "kaihui" literally says 'open a meeting'. Now listen to Xiaogu and Xiaoye's whole conversation again.
这杯苏打水是我熬夜的利器。
尝一下，尝了准不后悔！
请问，淳于总在哪儿？
求别说！
怎么了？
有些人的名字不能提，你提到他，他就会出现。
我们累到没有时间去写辞职信。
你是联合制作人的助理，跟我们不一样。
怎么不一样？
因为我们不用和他开会！
Just as Xiaoye warns her about attending meetings with Chun Yuqiao, Wang Er is about to call Xiaogu to prepare for one. You heard "qingwen", "zenme le", and "buyong" for "do not have to".
明天见！
